newsitem.title: USA: Carnival bars solo minors on cruises.
newsitem.headline: Carnival bars solo minors on cruises.

text.p: Carnival Corp's Carnival Cruise Lines calls itself the world's most popular cruise line, but the company said Friday it has had enough of its popularity with one class of cruise ship passengers -- people under age 21 travelling without an adult.

A Carnival official said Friday that, starting with sailings on February 6, 1997, any passenger under the age of 21 must be accompanied in the same state room by another person aged 25 or older. "Some of the people who were under 18, travelling alone, they tended to get boisterous," he said, explaining the reason for the policy shift.
Carnival executives were not immediately available to comment further. But the official said the number of people who would be affected by the change is "a very small percentage of passengers."
"It's not going to affect our bookings at all," he said.
Carnival's Holland America Line, Windstar Cruises and Seabourne Cruise Line are not affected by the policy shift.
